symbols.name: V
symbols.type: A finite labelled set of observed micro-variables.
symbols.role: Micro-variable index set.

symbols.name: n
symbols.type: A positive integer.
symbols.role: Number of micro-variables.

symbols.name: d
symbols.type: A finite-alphabet cardinality map.
symbols.role: Prescribed micro-alphabet sizes.

symbols.name: A
symbols.type: The joint observed alphabet.
symbols.role: Cell index set for complete observed laws.

symbols.name: C
symbols.type: A known partition of \(V\) into nonempty clusters.
symbols.role: Macro-variable system.

symbols.name: k
symbols.type: A positive integer.
symbols.role: Number of clusters.

symbols.name: pi
symbols.type: The known cluster-membership map.
symbols.role: Maps micro-variables to macro-variables.

symbols.name: H
symbols.type: A finite labelled directed mixed graph on the cluster set \(C\), possibly with directed cycles.
symbols.role: Arbitrary feasible cluster causal diagram.

symbols.name: EX
symbols.type: A set of intervention clusters.
symbols.role: Macro intervention coordinates.

symbols.name: EY
symbols.type: A nonempty set of outcome clusters.
symbols.role: Macro outcome coordinates.

symbols.name: X
symbols.type: The micro intervention set.
symbols.role: Micro-variables jointly set by a macro intervention.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.type: The micro outcome set.
symbols.role: Micro-variables reported by the target distribution.

symbols.name: cx
symbols.type: A macro intervention value.
symbols.role: Value assigned jointly to every micro-variable in the intervention clusters.

symbols.name: cy
symbols.type: A macro outcome value.
symbols.role: Cell of the macro outcome distribution.

symbols.name: G
symbols.type: A labelled directed mixed graph on \(V\).
symbols.role: Generic micrograph.

symbols.name: coarsen
symbols.type: The exact cluster-coarsening map.
symbols.def: \(K\to L\) or \(K\leftrightarrow L\) occurs in \(\operatorname{clust}_{C}(G)\) exactly when an edge of that type occurs in \(G\) between some labelled vertices in \(K\) and \(L\); declared self-loops use the same existential convention within a cluster.
symbols.role: Defines exact compatibility between micrographs and the cluster diagram.

symbols.name: R
symbols.type: The finite class of compatible micro-refinements.
symbols.role: Refinement uncertainty set.

symbols.name: M
symbols.type: A finite recursive semi-Markovian structural causal model on \(V\).
symbols.role: Generic compatible causal model.

symbols.name: GM
symbols.type: The active observed ADMG of \(M\).
symbols.def: \(G_M\) contains exactly the directed functional dependences and shared latent-root dependences active in \(M\).
symbols.role: Exact micrograph induced by the SCM.

symbols.name: PM
symbols.type: The complete observational law induced by \(M\).
symbols.role: Observed-data law.

symbols.name: QM
symbols.type: The full macro interventional distribution induced by \(M\).
symbols.role: Causal target under one SCM.

symbols.name: MH
symbols.type: The class of compatible finite SCMs.
symbols.role: Semantic model class for global identification.

symbols.name: p
symbols.type: A strictly positive observed cell-probability vector.
symbols.role: Generic complete observed law.

symbols.name: OmegaG
symbols.type: The strictly positive observable-law image of one refinement.
symbols.role: Domain on which a refinement-specific identifying functional is valid.

symbols.name: OmegaH
symbols.type: The union observable-law image of the cluster input.
symbols.role: Domain of a uniform macro-effect functional.

symbols.name: fG
symbols.type: An independently quantified refinement-local target map.
symbols.role: Semantic local identifying map used in the finite-union gluing criterion, independently of any algorithmic representation.

symbols.name: ID
symbols.type: The ordinary complete ID algorithm for one ADMG.
symbols.role: Refinement-local identification engine.

symbols.name: phiG
symbols.type: A refinement-specific rational target vector when ordinary ID succeeds.
symbols.role: Local identifying functional.

symbols.name: Guard
symbols.type: A finite conjunction of polynomial equalities and strict polynomial inequalities in the cells of \(p\).
symbols.role: Branch domain certificate for a guarded circuit.

symbols.name: Circuit
symbols.type: A finite guarded arithmetic directed acyclic graph.
symbols.role: Permitted symbolic output language.

symbols.name: F
symbols.type: A guarded arithmetic circuit with one output for every \((c_x,c_y)\).
symbols.role: Positive output of the conditional Global-CID composition.

symbols.name: Eval
symbols.type: Guarded-circuit evaluation.
symbols.def: For \(p\in\Omega_H\), \(\operatorname{Eval}(F,p)=F_b(p)\) for any branch \(b\) whose guard contains \(p\); guard coverage ensures existence, and the certified common-value condition on every overlap makes the value independent of the chosen branch. Evaluation shares common subexpressions and divides only by denominators certified positive on the chosen guard.
symbols.role: Turns a returned circuit into the identified target vector.

symbols.name: B
symbols.type: A positive integer.
symbols.role: Candidate latent-root support benchmark for the bounded-collision open question.

symbols.name: Vstar
symbols.type: The four-vertex set in the excluded-regime collision.
symbols.role: Vertex-minimal micro-variable set for the adjacent-singleton-cycle example.

symbols.name: dstar
symbols.type: The binary alphabet map on the collision vertices.
symbols.role: Observed alphabet specification for the explicit witness.

symbols.name: Cstar
symbols.type: The three-cluster partition in the excluded-regime collision.
symbols.role: Smallest partition supporting a directed cycle with two adjacent singleton clusters.

symbols.name: Hstar
symbols.type: The explicit cyclic directed cluster graph on \(C_{\star}\).
symbols.def: \(H_{\star}\) has precisely \(K_a\to K_b\), \(K_a\to K_{cd}\), \(K_{cd}\to K_a\), \(K_b\to K_{cd}\), and \(K_{cd}\to K_b\), with no bidirected edges.
symbols.role: Excluded cyclic cluster input for the strict collision result.

symbols.name: G1star
symbols.type: The first explicit acyclic micro-refinement.
symbols.def: \(G_{1\star}=\{c\to a,c\to b,a\to b,a\to d,b\to d\}\), with topological order \(c,a,b,d\).
symbols.role: First active DAG in the common-law collision.

symbols.name: G2star
symbols.type: The second explicit acyclic micro-refinement.
symbols.def: \(G_{2\star}=\{d\to a,d\to b,a\to b,a\to c,b\to c\}\), with topological order \(d,a,b,c\).
symbols.role: Second active DAG in the common-law collision.

symbols.name: pstar
symbols.type: The explicit strictly positive binary law shared by the two refinements.
symbols.role: Common complete observed law in the collision.

symbols.name: M1star
symbols.type: The finite recursive SCM obtained from the \(G_{1\star}\)-factorization of \(p_{\star}\).
symbols.role: First exact-active causal model in the collision.

symbols.name: M2star
symbols.type: The finite recursive SCM obtained from the \(G_{2\star}\)-factorization of \(p_{\star}\).
symbols.role: Second exact-active causal model in the collision.

symbols.name: EXstar
symbols.type: The intervention cluster set in the explicit collision.
symbols.role: Intervention coordinate of the excluded-regime query.

symbols.name: EYstar
symbols.type: The outcome cluster set in the explicit collision.
symbols.role: Outcome coordinate of the excluded-regime query.

symbols.name: ell
symbols.type: A positive integer.
symbols.def: \(\ell\) is the bit length of the labelled encoding of \((H,C,d,EX,EY)\).
symbols.role: Finite input length.

symbols.name: tower
symbols.type: The elementary tower family.
symbols.role: Complexity scale.

symbols.name: Bout
symbols.type: A positive integer.
symbols.role: Candidate elementary state-count, running-time, and output-length benchmark, conditional on the overlap-normal-form construction attaining it.

symbols.name: Certificate
symbols.type: A finite cross-refinement collision certificate.
symbols.role: Checkable negative output type, with the advertised uniform support bound posed as open.

symbols.name: Ops
symbols.type: The graph-native symbolic operation set.
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{Ops}\) consists of labelled refinement expansion, ordinary fixing and district decomposition, probability-ring normalization, splitting by graph-derived equality or positivity guards, arithmetic-DAG sharing, finite response-table compression, and exact checking of returned tables.
symbols.role: Allowed moves of the overlap normalizer; unrestricted real quantifier elimination is excluded.

symbols.name: OverlapState
symbols.type: A finite symbolic worklist state carrying labelled refinements, current fixing kernels, normalized arithmetic DAGs, guards, and unresolved refinement pairs.
symbols.role: State space of the overlap saturation, subject to the coverage, value-preservation, and no-lost-disagreement invariant in the overlap handle.

symbols.name: rank
symbols.type: A well-founded rank on overlap states.
symbols.sig: \(\rho:\mathsf{OverlapState}\to\mathbb N^m\) with lexicographic order for finite \(m\).
symbols.role: Termination certificate to be derived for the overlap normalizer.

symbols.name: GlobalCID
symbols.type: A deterministic formula-or-collision procedure parameterized by certified overlap and collision-compression subroutines.
symbols.role: Conditional composition of finite enumeration, ordinary ID, and the two certified open subroutines.

symbols.name: N
symbols.type: A positive sample size.
symbols.role: Number of independent observed draws.

symbols.name: Oi
symbols.type: Observed cell-valued random variables.
symbols.role: Sampling observations.

symbols.name: phat
symbols.type: The empirical multinomial law.
symbols.role: Plug-in input to a returned circuit.

symbols.name: S
symbols.type: A fixed positive-support stratum contained in one guard of \(F\).
symbols.role: Regular branch domain for influence inference.

symbols.name: U
symbols.type: An open neighborhood of \(p\) in the affine hull of the observed-law simplex.
symbols.role: Domain of the smooth stratum extension.

symbols.name: U0
symbols.type: A connected relatively open neighborhood of \(p\) contained in \(\mathcal U\cap\Delta^{\circ}(\mathcal A)\).
symbols.role: Ambient-simplex neighborhood on which the extension covariance has stable rank.

symbols.name: EN
symbols.type: The empirical rank-stability event.
symbols.role: High-probability event on which the empirical covariance has the population rank.

symbols.name: Ftilde
symbols.type: A continuously differentiable local extension of the active branch of \(F\) from \(S\) to an open neighborhood of \(p\).
symbols.role: Off-stratum evaluation used by the multinomial delta method.

symbols.name: JF
symbols.type: The Jacobian of the stratum extension.
symbols.role: Influence loading matrix.

symbols.name: psi
symbols.type: The multinomial influence vector of the active circuit branch.
symbols.def: \(\psi_p(a)=J_F(p)(e_a-p)\) for \(a\in\mathcal A\), where \(e_a\) is the cell basis vector.
symbols.role: First-order sampling fluctuation of the branch plug-in estimator.

symbols.name: Sigma
symbols.type: The local asymptotic covariance map of the smooth extension.
symbols.def: \(\Sigma_F(q)=J_F(q)\{\operatorname{diag}(q)-qq^{\mathsf T}\}J_F(q)^{\mathsf T}\) for \(q\in\mathcal U\); in particular, \(\Sigma_F(p)\) is the population covariance.
symbols.role: Ambient-simplex covariance map for regular-stratum Wald inference.

symbols.name: Sigmahat
symbols.type: The empirical circuit covariance matrix.
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Sigma_F=J_F(\widehat p_N)\{\operatorname{diag}(\widehat p_N)-\widehat p_N\widehat p_N^{\mathsf T}\}J_F(\widehat p_N)^{\mathsf T}\) when \(\widehat p_N\in\mathcal U\), and \(\widehat\Sigma_F=0\) otherwise.
symbols.role: Total plug-in covariance estimator whose zero fallback is used only outside the local extension neighborhood.

symbols.name: Qhat
symbols.type: The empirical-multinomial branch plug-in estimator.
symbols.def: \(\widehat Q_N=\widetilde F_S(\widehat p_N)\) when \(\widehat p_N\in\mathcal U\); otherwise, for every \(c_x\), set \(\widehat Q_N(c_y;c_x)=1/|\mathcal A_Y|\) for every \(c_y\).
symbols.role: Total estimator of the returned macro-effect functional; the fixed uniform fallback is asymptotically irrelevant on a regular stratum.

symbols.name: r
symbols.type: A nonnegative integer.
symbols.role: Effective dimension of the target contrast.

symbols.name: Theta
symbols.type: The target product-simplex.
symbols.role: Parameter space for the full collection of intervention-indexed outcome distributions.

symbols.name: alpha
symbols.type: A confidence error probability.
symbols.role: Nominal noncoverage level.

symbols.name: WN
symbols.type: The rank-adjusted Wald region.
symbols.def: Set \(\chi^2_{0,1-\alpha}:=0\). If \(r\ge1\), define \(\mathcal W_N=\{q\in\Theta:N(\widehat Q_N-q)^{\mathsf T}\widehat\Sigma_F^{+}(\widehat Q_N-q)\le\chi^2_{r,1-\alpha}\}\); if \(r=0\), define \(\mathcal W_N=\{\widehat Q_N\}\).
symbols.role: Regular-stratum confidence region.

symbols.name: epsilon
symbols.type: A nonnegative radius.
symbols.role: Simultaneous multinomial cell radius.

symbols.name: RN
symbols.type: A simultaneous confidence region for the observed law.
symbols.role: Finite-sample input region propagated through all guarded branches.

symbols.name: IN
symbols.type: A simultaneous target region.
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_N(F)=\operatorname{cl}\bigcup_b\{F_b(q):q\in R_N,\ g_b(q)\text{ holds, and every denominator of branch }b\text{ is positive}\}\), where \((g_b,F_b)\) ranges over the certified branches of \(F\).
symbols.role: Boundary-robust image of the multinomial region.

assumptions.condition: The directed part of \(G\) is acyclic.

standard.name: Exact compatibility with a cluster graph
Recursive SCM compatibility with a cluster refinement

assumptions.condition: For every \(v\in V\), the endogenous domain of \(v\) in \(M\) has cardinality \(d(v)\).

novel.justification: This intentional paper-specific restriction focuses the compiler and its inference layer on full-support finite observed laws. It is satisfied whenever every observable configuration has nonzero probability, as in finite discrete models with nondegenerate response noise, and it excludes boundary singularities without supplying the overlap-identification conclusion.

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_N\) are independent with common law \(p\) on \(\mathcal A\).

There exists a connected relatively open neighborhood \(\mathcal U_0\subseteq\mathcal U\cap\Delta^{\circ}(\mathcal A)\) containing \(p\) such that \(\operatorname{rank}\{\Sigma_F(q)\}=r\) for every \(q\in\mathcal U_0\), where \(\Sigma_F(q)\) is computed from the ambient-simplex extension \(\widetilde F_S\).

novel.justification: This paper-specific ambient matrix regularity holds for smooth branches whose Jacobian, after projection onto multinomial simplex-tangent directions, has locally constant effective rank. It is the sufficient condition used for elementary continuity of the covariance Moore--Penrose pseudoinverse and fixed-rank Wald asymptotics.

definitions.name: Compatible micro-refinement class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak R(H)=\{G\in\mathsf{DMG}(V):G\text{ has acyclic directed part and }\operatorname{clust}_{C}(G)=H\}\).

definitions.name: Compatible positive finite SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M(H,d)=\{M\in\mathsf{RSM}_{\mathrm{fin}}(V):G_M\in\mathfrak R(H),\ |\operatorname{dom}_M(v)|=d(v)\text{ for every }v\in V,\text{ and }P_M(a)>0\text{ for every }a\in\mathcal A\}\).

definitions.name: Global uniform identification
definitions.construction: The target is uniformly identified when there exists \(f:\Omega_H\to\Delta(\mathcal A_Y)^{\mathcal A_X}\) such that \(f(P_M)(c_y;c_x)=Q_M(c_y;c_x)\) for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,d)\) and every \((c_x,c_y)\).

definitions.name: Refinement-local ID functional
definitions.construction: For \(G\in\mathfrak R(H)\), run ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}(G,X,Y)\); on success, store its shared rational arithmetic DAG as \(\phi_G\), with every denominator accompanied by its positive-law guard.

definitions.name: Guarded arithmetic circuit
definitions.construction: A circuit is a finite list \(F=((g_b,F_b))_{b=1}^m\) in which each \(g_b\) is a guard, each \(F_b\) is an arithmetic DAG over rational constants and cells \(p(a)\) using \(+,-,\times,/\) and finite sums, the guards cover \(\Omega_H\), every divisor is strictly positive on its branch domain, and \(F_b(p)=F_{b'}(p)\) whenever \(p\in\Omega_H\) satisfies both \(g_b\) and \(g_{b'}\). For \(p\in\Omega_H\), \(\operatorname{Eval}(F,p)\) is this common value for any satisfied guard, so evaluation is total and independent of branch choice even when guards overlap.

definitions.name: Adjacent-singleton cyclic quotient and exact refinements
definitions.construction: Take \(V_{\star}=\{a,b,c,d\}\), binary alphabets, and \(C_{\star}=\{K_a,K_b,K_{cd}\}\) with \(K_a=\{a\}\), \(K_b=\{b\}\), and \(K_{cd}=\{c,d\}\). Let \(H_{\star}\) have exactly the directed edges \(K_a\to K_b\), \(K_a\to K_{cd}\), \(K_{cd}\to K_a\), \(K_b\to K_{cd}\), and \(K_{cd}\to K_b\), and no bidirected edges. Set \(G_{1\star}=\{c\to a,c\to b,a\to b,a\to d,b\to d\}\) with order \(c,a,b,d\), and \(G_{2\star}=\{d\to a,d\to b,a\to b,a\to c,b\to c\}\) with order \(d,a,b,c\). Finally set \(EX_{\star}=\{K_a\}\) and \(EY_{\star}=\{K_b\}\).

definitions.name: Common strictly positive law
definitions.construction: Define \(p_{\star}\) through the \(G_{1\star}\)-factorization by \(p_{\star}(c=1)=1/2\), \(p_{\star}(a=1\mid c=0)=1/4\), \(p_{\star}(a=1\mid c=1)=3/4\), \([p_{\star}(b=1\mid a,c)]_{(a,c)}=((1/8,3/8),(5/8,7/8))\), and \([p_{\star}(d=1\mid a,b)]_{(a,b)}=((1/5,2/5),(3/5,4/5))\), using complements for value zero and row-major order for binary parent tuples. Equivalently, the same law has the \(G_{2\star}\)-factorization \(p_{\star}(d=1)=1/2\), \([p_{\star}(a=1\mid d)]_{d=0,1}=(19/80,61/80)\), \([p_{\star}(b=1\mid a,d)]_{(a,d)}=((9/61,6/19),(13/19,52/61))\), and \([p_{\star}(c=1\mid a,b)]_{(a,b)}=((5/26,1/2),(1/2,21/26))\).

definitions.name: Exact-active finite SCM realizations of the common law
definitions.construction: For \(j\in\{1,2\}\), construct \(M_{j\star}\) in the displayed topological order of \(G_{j\star}\) by assigning one independent finite uniform exogenous variable to each observed vertex and using the inverse-CDF response table from the corresponding conditional probability in \(p_{\star}\). For \(M_{1\star}\), use uniform support sizes \(2,4,8,5\) for the response tables of \(c,a,b,d\). For \(M_{2\star}\), use uniform support sizes \(2,80,1159,26\) for the response tables of \(d,a,b,c\). Set a binary child to one exactly on the initial segment whose size equals its displayed success probability times the relevant support size.

definitions.name: Candidate bounded common-law collision certificate
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{Certificate}=(G_1,G_2,M_1,M_2,p,c_x,c_y)\) with \(G_j\in\mathfrak R(H)\), \(M_j\in\mathfrak M(H,d)\), \(G_{M_j}=G_j\), \(P_{M_1}=P_{M_2}=p\), \(Q_{M_1}(c_y;c_x)\neq Q_{M_2}(c_y;c_x)\), and every latent root of either model having support at most \(B(H,d)\); rational or real-algebraic table entries are encoded by integer polynomials and isolating intervals.

definitions.name: Paired response-table compression handle
definitions.construction: Start from any same-law pair witnessing failure of uniform identification. Replace each finite latent root by its deterministic response-type representation, couple the two observed-law moment systems through their common cell vector, and apply support reduction to the joint vector of observational cells, all macro intervention cells, active-edge contrasts, and normalization coordinates. The target is a pair that preserves the complete common observed law, every macro intervention distribution, strict positivity, prescribed observed alphabets, and both exact active micrographs while bounding each retained latent-root support by \(B(H,d)\).

definitions.name: Ranked fixing-overlap saturation handle
definitions.construction: After ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}(G,X,Y)\) has succeeded for every \(G\in\mathfrak R(H)\), start from \((G,\phi_G,\Omega_G)_{G\in\mathfrak R(H)}\) and design a finite worklist saturation using \(\mathsf{Ops}\). Every reachable overlap state must satisfy the following invariant: its guards form a finite cover of every feasible pair \((G,p)\) retained from the initial family; on each guarded piece, every stored fixing kernel and arithmetic DAG equals the corresponding \(\phi_G(p)\) on \(\Omega_G\); each unresolved refinement pair records precisely the common-law cells not yet certified equal or separated; and every transition preserves covered feasible pairs and cannot discard a cell on which two retained target values disagree. A terminal positive state is encoded as the finite list \(((g_b,F_b))_{b=1}^m\), with guard coverage, positive-divisor annotations, and pairwise common-value identities sufficient for \(\operatorname{Eval}\). A terminal negative state is encoded as a finite-support tuple \((G_1,G_2,M_1,M_2,p,c_x,c_y)\) together with topological-order, exact-coarsening, response-table, positivity, complete-law-equality, and target-separation checks, using integer-polynomial and isolating-interval encodings for real-algebraic entries; composition with a successful paired compressor adds the \(B(H,d)\) latent-support check. Derive a well-founded rank that strictly decreases after every nonterminal transition.

definitions.name: Conditional Global-CID composition
definitions.construction: Given a certified paired response-table compressor satisfying the collision-compression handle and a certified terminating saturation satisfying the ranked fixing-overlap handle, enumerate \(\mathfrak R(H)\) and run ordinary ID on every refinement. If a local run fails, apply the supplied compressor to its hedge witness. Otherwise apply the supplied saturation to the local formulas. Return the resulting common guarded circuit or cross-refinement collision certificate after exact checks of graph compatibility, positivity, full observed-law equality, branch coverage, overlap common-value identities, denominator safety, latent support, and target separation.

definitions.name: Empirical-multinomial branch plug-in estimator
definitions.construction: On \(\widehat p_N\in\mathcal U\), set \(\widehat Q_N=\widetilde F_S(\widehat p_N)\) and use the Jacobian plug-in covariance \(\widehat\Sigma_F\); outside \(\mathcal U\), set \(\widehat Q_N(c_y;c_x)=1/|\mathcal A_Y|\) for every \((c_x,c_y)\) and \(\widehat\Sigma_F=0\). Define \(E_N=\{\widehat p_N\in\mathcal U_0\}\). For \(r\ge1\), define \(\mathcal W_N\) over \(\Theta\) by the pseudoinverse quadratic inequality; for \(r=0\), set \(\chi^2_{0,1-\alpha}=0\) and \(\mathcal W_N=\{\widehat Q_N\}\). At the population law, the influence vector is \(\psi_p(a)=J_F(p)(e_a-p)\) and the covariance is \(\Sigma_F(p)\).

definitions.name: Guard-propagated simultaneous target region
definitions.construction: Construct \(R_N\) with radius \(\varepsilon_N\), then propagate every point of \(R_N\) through every circuit branch whose guard and denominator conditions it satisfies, and take the closure of the union to obtain \(\mathcal I_N(F)\).

statements.statement: The compatible refinement class is finite and can be enumerated from the labelled input, with \(|\mathfrak R(H)|\le 2^{3n(n-1)/2}\); every enumerated graph carries a topological ordering certificate for its directed part and an exact coarsening certificate.
statements.justification: Finiteness turns arbitrary clustering into a finite union problem without confusing a cyclic quotient with a cyclic micrograph.
statements.gap: AnandRibeiroTianBareinboim2023CDAG assumes an acyclic cluster graph and does not enumerate exact known-size micro-refinements for global identification when the supplied quotient is cyclic.
statements.consumer: It supplies the finite input family for the conditional enumeration layer and its explicit complexity accounting.

statements.statement: The macro target is uniformly identified over \(\mathfrak M(H,d)\) if and only if there exists an independently quantified family \((f_G)_{G\in\mathfrak R(H)}\), with \(f_G:\Omega_G\to\Delta(\mathcal A_Y)^{\mathcal A_X}\), such that \(f_G(P_M)=Q_M\) for every \(G\in\mathfrak R(H)\) and every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,d)\) satisfying \(G_M=G\), and \(f_{G_1}(p)=f_{G_2}(p)\) for every \(G_1,G_2\in\mathfrak R(H)\) and every \(p\in\Omega_{G_1}\cap\Omega_{G_2}\). When these conditions hold, \(f(p)=f_G(p)\) for any \(G\) with \(p\in\Omega_G\) is well defined on \(\Omega_H\). This statement does not require an algorithmic representation of \(f_G\).
statements.justification: This preliminary gluing fact isolates the semantic overlap obligation without claiming to solve its constructive representation problem.
statements.gap: TehSadeghiSoo2025RobustID gives a sufficient shared-expression criterion for candidate SA-MPDAGs; it does not characterize agreement only on common observable-law images of hidden-variable refinements.
statements.consumer: It supplies the correctness specification against which the ranked overlap saturation is judged.

statements.statement: Does every failure of uniform identification over \(\mathfrak M(H,d)\) admit a collision certificate in which every latent root has at most \(B(H,d)=2^n\prod_{v\in V}d(v)+4n^2+1\) states, while preserving the complete common observed law, all macro intervention distributions, strict observed positivity, prescribed alphabets, and both exact active micrographs? The Handle is the paired response-table compression that retains the joint observational, interventional, activity, and normalization coordinates before support reduction.
statements.justification: A general formula-or-collision theorem needs a finite inspectable witness theorem beyond the single explicit cyclic example.
statements.gap: ShpitserPearl2006JointID constructs a hedge pair for one fixed ADMG, and ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCF canonicalizes one fixed graph; neither jointly enforces a same-positive-law collision across two exact refinements with active advertised edges.
statements.consumer: A positive solution supplies the bounded negative-output subroutine used by the conditional Global-CID corollary.

statements.statement: For the binary input \(V_{\star}=\{a,b,c,d\}\), \(C_{\star}=\{K_a,K_b,K_{cd}\}\), \(H_{\star}\), \(EX_{\star}=\{K_a\}\), and \(EY_{\star}=\{K_b\}\) in the explicit construction, \(G_{1\star}\) and \(G_{2\star}\) are acyclic exact refinements of \(H_{\star}\). Their common skeleton contains every pair except \(c-d\), neither graph has an unshielded collider, and their common positive observational model is characterized by \(c\mathrel{\perp\!\!\!\perp}d\mid(a,b)\). The displayed law \(p_{\star}\) is strictly positive and factorizes over both graphs. The inverse-CDF models \(M_{1\star}\) and \(M_{2\star}\) have exact active graphs \(G_{1\star}\) and \(G_{2\star}\), respectively, and both induce \(p_{\star}\). Nevertheless, \(\Pr_{M_{1\star}}(b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(a=0))=1/4\) whereas \(\Pr_{M_{2\star}}(b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(a=0))=537/2318\), and \(\Pr_{M_{1\star}}(b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(a=1))=3/4\) whereas \(\Pr_{M_{2\star}}(b=1\mid\operatorname{do}(a=1))=1781/2318\); the differences are \(85/4636\) and \(-85/4636\). Every refinement of \(H_{\star}\) is a DAG and hence is locally identified, but the macro effect is not uniformly identified. This is vertex-minimal among feasible directed cycles containing two adjacent singleton clusters: a cycle consisting only of singleton clusters would force a directed micro-cycle, so three clusters and one additional vertex are necessary, and sizes \((1,1,2)\) attain the bound. Hence no single global uniform functional can represent the locally identified values. Consequently, any terminating saturation satisfying the ranked overlap handle and its exact equality-or-separation invariant must detect or reproduce a valid separating certificate for this input.

statements.statement: After ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}(G,X,Y)\) succeeds for every \(G\in\mathfrak R(H)\), can one construct the ranked fixing-overlap saturation specified by the handle using only \(\mathsf{Ops}\), with every reachable state satisfying its guard-cover, local-value preservation, exact unresolved-pair, and no-lost-disagreement invariant, and with every terminal state encoded either as a guarded circuit whose overlapping satisfied branches have one common \(\operatorname{Eval}\) value or as the fully checked finite-support tuple \((G_1,G_2,M_1,M_2,p,c_x,c_y)\) of a collision certificate? The construction must terminate, extract a disagreement-preserving witness on a negative branch, and return the circuit exactly when \(\phi_{G_1}=\phi_{G_2}\) on every nonempty \(\Omega_{G_1}\cap\Omega_{G_2}\). Composition with a solution to the bounded-collision question should enforce \(B(H,d)\). A further quantitative objective is to make the combined state count, bit complexity, and encoded terminal output at most \(B_{\mathrm{out}}(\ell)\); this \(E_4\) bound is conditional on a proved decreasing rank and transition and encoding bounds.
statements.justification: This constructive normal form is the sole non-routine bridge from semantic finite-union identification to a graph-native algorithm.
statements.gap: YvernesEtAl2026DerivationGraphs Theorem 6 and Section 4.5 give a bounded normal form for single conditional-interventional derivations in one ADMG, while Section 6 identifies finite representations of broader derivation spaces as an open direction; LeeSpekkens2017AlgebraicCausal supplies general elimination only for tiny finite functional structures.
statements.consumer: Solving it supplies the terminating compilation or separating-pair step required by Global-CID without relabelling unrestricted real quantifier elimination as causal identification.

statements.statement: Conditional on a paired response-table compressor satisfying the bounded-collision handle and a terminating saturation satisfying the ranked fixing-overlap handle, finite refinement enumeration, ordinary ID, and exact certificate checking yield Global-CID. It terminates on every feasible encoded input and returns exactly one of two checkable objects. A formula return is a guarded circuit \(F\) whose overlap common-value condition makes \(\operatorname{Eval}(F,P_M)\) total and satisfies \(\operatorname{Eval}(F,P_M)(c_y;c_x)=Q_M(c_y;c_x)\) simultaneously for every \(M\in\mathfrak M(H,d)\) and every \((c_x,c_y)\). A negative return is a collision certificate obeying \(B(H,d)\). The procedure returns a circuit if and only if the macro target is uniformly identified. If the supplied compressor and saturation additionally have state count, transition cost, and terminal encoding length within the quantitative objectives of the open questions, then the total bit complexity and encoded output length are at most \(B_{\mathrm{out}}(\ell)\).
statements.justification: This conditional corollary is routine bookkeeping once the two open subroutines provide compression and terminating overlap saturation with their stated guarantees.
statements.gap: It is not positioned as an advance over published completeness theorems: all non-routine constructive content is assigned to the two open questions, with the ranked fixing-overlap saturation as the sole headline solve target.
statements.consumer: After the open subroutines are proved, the ALARM grouping receives either one implementable functional or a fully checked pair of incompatible micro-level causal mechanisms.

statements.statement: For a circuit return and a fixed stratum \(S\), let \(E_N=\{\widehat p_N\in\mathcal U_0\}\). Strict positivity and multinomial consistency imply \(\Pr_p(E_N)\to1\). On \(E_N\), the total definitions coincide with \(\widehat Q_N=\widetilde F_S(\widehat p_N)\) and the Jacobian plug-in covariance, and \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat\Sigma_F)=r\) exactly. Hence, without conditioning, \(\widehat\Sigma_F\to\Sigma_F(p)\) and \(\widehat\Sigma_F^{+}\to\Sigma_F(p)^{+}\) in probability, while \(\sqrt N\{\widehat Q_N-\operatorname{Eval}(F,p)\}\) converges to \(\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_F(p))\) with influence vector \(\psi_p(O_i)=J_F(p)(e_{O_i}-p)\). If \(r\ge1\), then \(\Pr_p\{\operatorname{Eval}(F,p)\in\mathcal W_N\}\to1-\alpha\). If \(r=0\), the derivative of \(\widetilde F_S\) vanishes in every simplex-tangent direction throughout the connected neighborhood \(\mathcal U_0\), so \(\widetilde F_S\) is constant there and \(\Pr_p\{\operatorname{Eval}(F,p)\in\mathcal W_N\}\to1\).
statements.justification: A graphically identified circuit becomes empirically useful only after its branchwise sampling law and covariance are explicit.
statements.gap: BhattacharyaNabiShpitser2022Semiparametric derives influence estimators for one fixed graphical functional, not a circuit compiled across observable-model overlaps.
statements.consumer: The ALARM analysis obtains automatic-differentiation standard errors for every reported macro outcome coordinate on a certified regular stratum.

statements.statement: For every \(N\ge1\), every \(p\in\Omega_H\), and every circuit return, \(\Pr_p\{\operatorname{Eval}(F,p)\in\mathcal I_N(F)\}\ge1-\alpha\). The guarantee holds without selecting one empirical branch and remains valid at intersections of equality guards; any certified outer approximation to \(\mathcal I_N(F)\) inherits the same coverage.
statements.justification: Guard intersections are statistically nonregular, so honest inference must propagate uncertainty through all near-compatible branches rather than condition on a selected formula.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019DirectionalInference treats directionally differentiable maps, while the present region exploits finite multinomial concentration and certified guard coverage for a union of graphical model images.
statements.consumer: Applied users obtain a valid finite-sample target region when empirical ALARM cell frequencies lie near a structural or formula-agreement boundary.

sampling_model.design: Independent multinomial sampling from one fixed strictly positive compatible observed law \(p\).
sampling_model.treatment: The macro intervention \(\operatorname{do}(X=c_x)\) is the causal query and is not randomly assigned in the observational sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cell is strictly positive at the fixed law \(p\); this pointwise condition permits choosing a local positive neighborhood inside the simplex, and no uniform positive-margin class is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nonparametric nuisance is required: \(\widehat p_N\) is the empirical complete-cell law, circuit derivatives are obtained by arithmetic-DAG differentiation on \(\mathcal U\), the plug-in estimator uses a fixed uniform target vector and zero covariance outside \(\mathcal U\), covariance rank is stable on the connected ambient-simplex neighborhood \(\mathcal U_0\), and boundary inference propagates \(R_N\) through every certified guard.

technical_internal_limitation: The preliminary finite-union equivalence is semantic and quantifies refinement-local identifying maps independently; it does not itself provide ordinary-ID formulas or a guarded circuit. Raw rational comparison is unsound because two formulas may differ on the free simplex yet agree on the intersection of their refinement images. Conversely, separately constructed hedge witnesses need not share one observed law, and the union of acyclic witness refinements may contain a directed cycle. The ranked fixing-overlap normal form must preserve its guard-cover, local-value, exact-unresolved-pair, and no-lost-disagreement invariant until it produces the fully encoded positive or negative terminal certificate. The self-contained four-vertex collision proves an explicit same-law cross-refinement separation for \(H_{\star}\), but it proves neither general disagreement-preserving extraction nor the support bound \(B(H,d)\). FerreiraAssaad2025CDMGADMG Section 4, Figure 5 is acyclic and supplies no provenance for the cyclic example. Generic real quantifier elimination may check a terminal algebraic certificate but does not count as the overlap saturation, and the \(E_4\) bound is not asserted without the missing decreasing-rank, support-compression, and size analyses. Conditional Global-CID contains no independent non-routine step once those ingredients are available.
honest_scope: The preliminary semantic gluing lemma, finite refinement enumeration, explicit same-law four-vertex collision, and multinomial inference reductions have direct proof routes. The gluing lemma uses independently quantified semantic maps; \(\phi_G\) is introduced only after ordinary ID succeeds. FerreiraAssaad2025CDMGADMG Section 4, Figure 5 displays the acyclic C-DAG \(C_w\to C_x\), \(C_w\to C_y\), and \(C_x\to C_y\) and is not the direct comparator for the new cyclic quotient \(H_{\star}\). The proposition claims the independently checked common-positive-law disagreement across two exact refinements and its consequence for global uniform identification. The constructive overlap normal form is the sole headline solve target: its saturation invariant and terminal encodings are specified, but a decreasing rank, finite guard coverage, exact overlap equality or separation, disagreement-preserving witness extraction, and size analysis must still be supplied. General paired collision compression and its \(B(H,d)\) support guarantee are open support work; the explicit example does not prove them. The Global-CID proposition and the \(B_{\mathrm{out}}(\ell)\) complexity and output guarantee are conditional corollaries of solutions to both construction questions. The smooth-stratum theorem is a regular-extension result requiring covariance-rank stability on an ambient-simplex neighborhood; equality-guard boundary behavior without that neighborhood condition belongs to the separate simultaneous-region theorem. The result intentionally restricts attention to complete macro interventions on known clusters in finite recursive semi-Markovian SCMs with exact graph activity and strictly positive observed laws; it does not identify micro interventions, cyclic micro-SCM effects, or clinical efficacy. On acyclic C-DAGs and singleton partitions, the conditional procedure must reduce to published cluster ID and ordinary ID. The vertex-minimality claim is only for a feasible directed cycle containing two adjacent singleton clusters; a smaller \((1,2)\) example exists for a cycle containing merely one singleton cluster.

literature_checklist.author: Simon Ferreira and Charles K. Assaad
literature_checklist.one_line: Section 4, Figure 5 displays the acyclic C-DAG with edges Cw to Cx, Cw to Cy, and Cx to Cy; it is background rather than the direct comparator for the new cyclic collision.

literature_checklist.author: Kai Z. Teh, Kayvan Sadeghi, and Terry Soo
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 2 gives a sufficient robust-identification criterion across candidate SA-MPDAGs.

literature_checklist.author: Clément Yvernes, Emilie Devijver, Marianne Clausel, and Eric Gaussier
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 6 and Section 4.5 give a single-ADMG derivation normal form, while Section 6 motivates broader finite-representation questions.

literature_checklist.author: Ciarán M. Lee and Robert W. Spekkens
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorem 1 and Section 6 develop finite algebraic causal feasibility tests and describe the scaling barrier of generic elimination.

literature_checklist.author: Junzhe Zhang, Jin Tian, and Elias Bareinboim
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 1 and 2 provide finite canonical SCMs and sharp polynomial bounds for one fixed causal diagram.

literature_checklist.author: Rohit Bhattacharya, Razieh Nabi, and Ilya Shpitser
literature_checklist.one_line: Fixing-derived functionals are translated into influence-function and weighting estimators for one ADMG; the paper-specific rank condition is not attributed to this source.

literature_checklist.author: Zheng Fang and Andres Santos
literature_checklist.one_line: Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 characterize bootstrap failure and derivative-aware resampling for directionally differentiable maps.

literature_checklist.author: Tara V. Anand and George Hripcsak
literature_checklist.one_line: The ALARM study operationalizes C-DAG effect analysis under deliberately coarse medical domain knowledge.
